lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl \u003cb\u003econju:
"

When double bonds are conjugated, the π orbitals delocalize and move closer together: the HOMO–LUMO gap decreases and absorption shifts to a longer wavelength (bathochromic effect). Increase the number of double bonds and watch λmax rise from 165 nm into the visible region.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCuando λmax entra en:
"

When λmax enters the visible range (400–700 nm) the substance looks colored, with the complementary color of the light it absorbs: β-carotene absorbs blue (~450 nm) and looks orange. Below 400 nm the substance is colorless even though it absorbs UV.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003eabsor:
"

Absorbance follows the Beer–Lambert law: A = ε·c·l, where ε is the molar absorption coefficient (it increases with conjugation), c the concentration and l the path length. An A between 0.1 and 1 is the useful range for measurement.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa espectroscopía \u0:
"

UV-Vis spectroscopy measures the absorption of light that promotes electrons from an occupied orbital to an empty one. In an alkene, the transition is π → π*: the electron goes from the HOMO to the LUMO. The photon energy must match the gap: E = hc/λ. Ethene absorbs at ~165 nm (far UV).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos \u003cb\u003esust:
"

Each alkyl substituent attached to the sp² carbons shifts λmax by about +5 nm, according to the Woodward–Fieser rules. Add substituents and compare. Groups with lone pairs (auxochromes such as –OR, –NR₂) produce even larger shifts.

"
